clue.text: Refinement in one of classy speech, on the surface about fifty

indicators.note: the classy word lies on the outside, wrapped around the numerals like a skin

parts.note: posh is an informal word for upper-class, so posh speech is the classy accent
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A remark on someone's refined accent, oddly measured as about fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: The Roman numerals L and I sit inside POSH, with 'on the surface about' telling you the posh word goes round them.
explanation.definitionFit: Polish as a noun is the refinement or elegance of manner of a cultivated person.

clue.text: Part of speech could have means to unite to produce manifesto

indicators.note: the answer is what would be left, the thing that could take on the binder
adding the binder would produce the manifesto word, so take it away from that word

parts.note: a manifesto is a public declaration or formal statement
cement is a binding material, a means of joining things together

explanation.surface: A grammarian noting that a word could unite with others to make a political manifesto.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: the answer plus CEMENT makes PRONOUNCEMENT, so remove CEMENT from it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pronoun such as 'she' or 'it' is one of the classes of words in grammar.

clue.text: Heads to location of clinics, unusual medic

definitions.text: Heads to location of clinics, unusual medic

indicators.note: heads are the leading letters, so take the first letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A rare doctor heads off to wherever the clinics are.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: a locum is the unusual, visiting doctor who heads to whichever clinic needs cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A locum is a stand-in doctor temporarily covering for another, so not the usual medic.

clue.text: Support for Spooner's curious loss of energy

indicators.note: curious means strange or odd, telling you to rearrange the remaining letters
loss means the energy letter is taken away from the name

parts.note: the name of the Oxford don is used here just for its letters, possessive s included
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Backing for a reverend gentleman's odd lack of vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: No sound swap here, though Spooner is named: his name is plain fodder (the fifteensquared blog parses it the same way). Remove E to leave SPOONRS, and 'curious' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: To sponsor someone is to back or support them, especially with money.

clue.text: Cheered upper-class damsel endlessly in distress

indicators.note: distress suggests things being knocked out of shape, signalling a rearrangement
endlessly means the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A posh damsel in distress was rescued and cheered up, rather like a fairy tale.
explanation.walkthrough: DAMSE (damsel with its end cut off) joins U, and 'in distress' rearranges UDAMSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being amused is being entertained or made happy, so cheered in that sense.

clue.text: Use dark words of medium, so to speak

parts.note: M is the clothing-size abbreviation for medium
to utter something is to speak it

explanation.surface: A spiritualist medium speaks ominous words at a seance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'medium' looks like a psychic, but it is just M, the size.
explanation.definitionFit: To mutter is to grumble under your breath, often voicing dark complaints.

clue.text: Woman stretched out on top of taxi, without a second thought for wool-producer's problem

indicators.note: without means outside, so the woman and the taxi go around the second thought
in a down answer, on top of means placed above the following part

parts.note: the pronoun she with its last letter drawn out an extra step
a cab is a taxi
PS, postscript, is a second thought added after a letter

explanation.surface: A woman lounging on a taxi roof gives no thought to a farmer's flock trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without a second thought' reads as the idiom for acting rashly, but 'without' means outside, and a second thought is a postscript.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheep scab is a skin disease caused by mites that afflicts the animals bred for wool.

clue.text: Immoveable, fixed, sedated

indicators.note: fixed in the sense of rigged or doctored, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient who is sedated lies fixed and unable to move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixed' reads as a synonym of the definition but it signals the rearrangement of SEDATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dead set on something is utterly determined, unshakeable in their resolve.

clue.text: Read about African country to the east of this gulf, where you may go no further

definitions.text: where you may go no further
definitions.note: a clause describing a place, while the answer is the verb phrase of arriving at one

indicators.note: about means the reading word goes round the country, compass point and gulf

parts.note: taken as written
Chad is a landlocked country in north-central Africa
the Gulf of Aden lies east of Africa, between Somalia and Yemen

explanation.surface: Instructions to read up on a country lying east of a particular gulf, at the end of the road.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the situation rather than the act: to reach a dead end is to arrive at a point you can go no further.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead end is a road closed at one end, so reaching one means progress is impossible.

clue.text: Speaking of speech: "To arms, fair band!"

indicators.note: speaking signals that the word for speech is said aloud, and in a non-rhotic accent it matches the answer

parts.note: talk is speech

explanation.surface: A rousing call to arms addressed to a fair band of warriors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To arms' is surface colour: in standard British pronunciation, without a sounded R, TALK and TORC sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A torc is an ornamental metal neck ring of the ancient Celts, a decorative band.

clue.text: Biko's last part of speech about the African rights leaders gives trajectory of wasted shot

indicators.note: last means take only the final letter of the activist's name
about means the grammatical word goes round the article

parts.note: a verb is a part of speech
taken as written

indicators.note: leaders are the first letters of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A speech by Steve Biko, South African anti-apartheid campaigner, about African rights leaders.
explanation.walkthrough: Steve Biko was a South African anti-apartheid activist; only the final O of his name is used. VERB goes 'about' THE.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot over the bar sails above the crossbar of the goal, the path of a missed attempt in football or rugby.

clue.text: See 21
Free speech, at a price? That's less costly than the alternatives

indicators.note: free here means loosened, so the letters are set free to rearrange

explanation.surface: If free speech comes at a price, it might still be the cheapest option going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free' looks like part of 'free speech' but it signals the rearrangement of SPEECHAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheapest option is the one costing least compared with all others.

clue.text: He leads speakers on march: an order goes out

indicators.note: putting things in order means arranging them, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A protest leader at the head of a march gives an order to go out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes out' is only surface colour; the definition is a cryptic picture of a newsreader introducing the other broadcasters.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchorman presents a broadcast and introduces the other reporters and contributors.

clue.text: Gave eerie haunted house party

indicators.note: to house is to contain, so the party goes inside the rearranged letters
eerie suggests something strange, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: do is an informal British word for a party

explanation.surface: A Halloween host threw a party in a spooky haunted house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house' looks like part of 'haunted house' but is the verb to contain; 'eerie' makes HANDEUT from the haunted letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To hand something out is to distribute or give it to people.

clue.text: Last part of speech is in French and authentic German

indicators.note: is in means the end of speech is placed inside the French word

parts.note: et is the French word for and
the final two letters of the word speech

explanation.surface: A linguistic remark that a word's ending is shared by French and genuine German.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last part of speech' gives the last two letters, CH, not just the final H.
explanation.definitionFit: Echt is a German word for genuine, borrowed into English for something authentic.

clue.text: Lack power of speech? That's insincere

definitions.meaning: to be unable to do something, the contraction of cannot
hypocritical, sanctimonious talk, or the jargon of a group

explanation.surface: Someone who cannot speak, and a suspicion that their words are hollow.
explanation.definitionFit: Can't means cannot, lacking the ability; cant is hypocritical pious talk.

clue.text: Tackle bluff incline

parts.note: a con is a swindle or bluff
to incline towards something is to tend to it

explanation.surface: A rugby or hiking image of tackling a steep cliff slope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bluff' and 'incline' both pose as landscape nouns, but one means deceive and the other lean.
explanation.definitionFit: To contend with a problem is to grapple with or deal with it, to take it on.

clue.text: Boatman has worth, but first he gets a page of insult

indicators.note: but first means the pronoun and page go ahead of the rest

parts.note: an AB, able seaman, is a sailor; also the setter's own pseudonym
use means worth or value, as in 'of no use'

explanation.surface: The setter boasts of his worth, but first gets an insulting page of complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: Boatman is the setter, but here the word gives AB, a sailor (able seaman).
explanation.definitionFit: To heap abuse on someone is to pile insults on them, so to insult heavily.

clue.text: Call Boatman for a bit of a talk

parts.note: to phone someone is to call them
the setter, Boatman, refers to himself, so me

explanation.surface: An invitation to ring the setter for a short chat.
explanation.definitionFit: A phoneme is the smallest unit of sound in spoken language, a tiny piece of speech.

clue.text: Speech about a dog

indicators.note: about means the speech word goes around the article

parts.note: a spiel is a glib speech or patter
an is the form of the indefinite article before a vowel

explanation.surface: A talk given on the subject of a canine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' gives AN, the other form of the indefinite article.
explanation.definitionFit: A spaniel is a breed of gun dog with long drooping ears.

clue.text: Flowery organ, one in canon ending at prayers

parts.note: St, saint, is one in the canon of recognised saints
amen is said at the end of a prayer

explanation.surface: A church organ with flowery decoration, played by a canon at the end of prayers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' looks like the church instrument; 'Flowery' turns it into part of a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The stamen is the pollen-producing male reproductive organ of a flower.

clue.text: Speech marks radically converted imams?

indicators.note: radically means thoroughly changed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about religious leaders converted to a radically different faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'radically' rearranges the fourteen letters of CONVERTED IMAMS.
explanation.definitionFit: Inverted commas are the punctuation marks that enclose quoted speech.

clue.text: A bit of a laugh in porn version of Oliver!?

definitions.note: a person, the boy hero of Dickens's novel and the musical

indicators.note: in means the laugh is placed inside the rearranged letters
a version is a rearranged rendering, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: ha is a single burst of laughter

explanation.surface: A joke about a smutty remake of the musical Oliver!
explanation.walkthrough: 'version' makes ORPN; the '!?' nods to the title of the musical Oliver! and to the absurdity of the idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Twist, the hero of Dickens's novel and the musical Oliver!, is a parentless boy raised in a workhouse.

clue.text: Silence is a part of speech

indicators.note: of speech means the word for a part is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: a piece is a part or portion

explanation.surface: A grammarian's claim that silence is a part of speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of speech' looks like a grammatical term, but 'of speech' signals the sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Peace means quiet or tranquillity, as in 'peace and quiet'.

clue.text: Scout takes in warning about starting motor launch again

indicators.note: takes in means the scouting word contains what follows

parts.note: recce is informal for reconnaissance, a scouting mission

indicators.note: about means the warning goes around the letter

parts.note: an omen is a warning sign

indicators.note: starting means just the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A scout picks up a warning about starting a motor launch again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'launch' poses as a boat; it is the verb meaning start. OMEN goes 'about' M; RECCE 'takes in' the result.
explanation.definitionFit: To recommence is to begin again, to relaunch something halted.

clue.text: Eager to help frame part of speech

indicators.note: to frame is to surround, so the help word goes around the letter

parts.note: aid is help
V is the abbreviation for verb, a part of speech

explanation.surface: Someone keen to help frame a grammatical part.
explanation.definitionFit: An avid reader or fan is keen and enthusiastic.

clue.text: Disjointed noun used in scary process of meeting a new partner!

definitions.text: process of meeting a new partner

indicators.note: split the word noun into two pieces and it reads 'no un', an instruction to drop those letters

parts.note: daunting means intimidating or scary

explanation.surface: A grammatical word wedged into the intimidating ritual of finding a new romance.
explanation.walkthrough: Joke: break 'noun' apart and it says NO UN, so take UN out of DAUNTING.
explanation.definitionFit: Dating is going out with people romantically to find or get to know a partner.

clue.text: Revoke authentic record holder

indicators.note: holder means the genuine word holds the record inside it

parts.note: real means authentic or genuine
EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A demand to cancel the title of a genuine record holder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record holder' reads as a champion, but it means REAL holding EP.
explanation.definitionFit: To repeal a law is to revoke or cancel it officially.
